name: Hanan
overview: Hanan was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant and played a key role in explaining the law to the people. He is mentioned in the context of the post-exilic community, notably appearing on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10:10. His service highlights his involvement in both religious duties and teaching during the restoration period.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanan means "gracious" in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name used in the biblical text. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries the connotation of grace as understood in the original language.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hanan as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hanan's significance lies in his dual role as a temple servant and as an instructor of the law, which was vital for the spiritual renewal of Israel after the exile. His inclusion on the sealed covenant document underscores his commitment to the community's covenantal obligations. Through his teaching, he contributed to the people's understanding and observance of God's law, supporting the restoration of proper worship and obedience.
